headline: Daily Access Permits and Beach Reservations
reservation: Parc national d'Oka requires a daily access permit which should be purchased online in advance to guarantee entry, especially for the beach sector. Entry permits are separate from camping or cabin reservations; during peak summer weekends, the park may reach capacity early.

days.title: Lac des Deux Montagnes Waters

stops.name: Grande Pointe Beach
stops.detail: Enjoy the supervised swimming areas and the expansive sandy shoreline of the lake.

stops.name: La Grande Baie Trail
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk through marshlands to observe the local flora and wetland bird species.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour from the city; traffic on the Galipeault Bridge can vary.
days.note: Beach access is heavily weather-dependent and subject to water quality testing.

days.title: Summit Views and History

stops.name: Calvaire d'Oka
stops.detail: Hike the historic trail featuring four oratories and three chapels built in the 18th century.

stops.name: Le Sommet Lookout
stops.detail: Gain a panoramic view of the Lac des Deux Montagnes and the Adirondacks in the distance.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes between park sectors; walking between trails is common.
days.note: The Calvaire trail involves moderate inclines; allow extra time for the descent.

days.title: Winter Trails or Autumn Foliage

stops.name: L'Écureuil Trail
stops.detail: Cycle or snowshoe through the mature forest depending on the season.

stops.name: Park Interpretation Centre
stops.detail: Review the ecological history of the region and the transformation of the sandy terraces.

days.driving: Allow 20 to 30 minutes; winter road clearing is frequent but check conditions.
days.note: Fatbike and ski rentals are seasonal and managed at the Le Littoral service center.

intel.title: Beach Sector Capacity
intel.text: The main beach lot is large but fills quickly on warm weekends; arrive early to secure a spot near the water. Additional parking is available at the Calvaire trailhead for hikers.

intel.title: Network Reliability
intel.text: Cellular signal is strong throughout most of the park due to its proximity to Montreal. Some depressions in the Calvaire d'Oka trail may experience minor signal drops.

intel.title: Local Services
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are readily available in the village of Oka or nearby Saint-Eustache. There are no fueling stations within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Peak Beach Hours
intel.text: Supervised swimming typically begins at 10 AM; check the Sépaq website for specific seasonal lifeguard schedules. The park remains open for hiking until sunset.

intel.title: Cyclist Connectivity
intel.text: The park is connected to the Route Verte, making it highly accessible for long-distance cyclists. Check for shared-path etiquette between walkers and bikers on the shoreline trails.

plan.arrival: Drive from YUL airport via Autoroute 640 West; stop in Saint-Eustache for major grocery runs before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are sufficient; the park has designated areas for RVs in the camping sectors.
plan.goldenHour: The Le Sommet viewpoint offers the best vantage point for watching the sun set over the lake.
